chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu al-Yasa', from Abu Shibl, who said:

Safwan said, 'And I do not know except that I have heard from Abu Shibl, that: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever loves you for what you are upon, he will enter Paradise, even if he did not say as you say.'

key_terms.عَلَى مَا أَنْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ: upon what you are upon (referring to their spiritual status/Wilayah)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for entering Paradise through love of the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the primacy of internal conviction (Wilayah) over external ritualistic uniformity, a key tenet in Shia theology distinguishing substantive loyalty from mere formalism. It underscores that genuine love for the Ahl al-Bayt, rooted in recognizing their divine station, is the decisive criterion for Paradise, regardless of minor differences in verbal expressions or practices among followers.
